(https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-TTS/blob/022e286b98fbec7e1e916cb940cdf532cd9f488e/qwen_tts/cli/de… Command: Documented Python voice-clone snippet wrapped as a uv one-liner; device_map changed from 'cuda:0' to 'cpu' (official CLI help lists cpu as a device_map value); attn_implementation='flash_attention_2' dropped (the card marks flash-attn 'Optional: for optimized performance' and it is GPU-only); gb is the sum of the weight files the command loads (model.safetensors 3.86 GB; model.safetensors 0.68 GB); runtime memory is higher. name: ABR asr-19m-v2-en

variants.cmd: uvx --from huggingface_hub hf download abr-ai/niagara-19m-batch.en --revision dab6545337495482f2fc05455432a7a05c88d3cc --local-dir asr-19m-v2-en && uv run --with torch --with transformers --with sentencepiece --with soundfile python -c "import soundfile as sf; from transformers import AutoFeatureExtractor, AutoModel, AutoTokenizer; p = './asr-19m-v2-en'; feature_extractor = AutoFeatureExtractor.from_pretrained(p, trust_remote_code=True); model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(p, trust_remote_code=True); tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(p, trust_remote_code=True); audio, _ = sf.read('audio.wav', dtype='float32'); print(tokenizer.decode_from_logits(model(feature_extractor(audio)))[0])"
variants.note: transformers remote code (trust_remote_code) at the evaluated revision, wrapping a TorchScript checkpoint. Platform evidence: model.py at dab6545: "device = \"cuda\" if torch.cuda.is_available() else \"cpu\"" and "filename = f\"{self.config.torchscript_model_file}-{device}.pt\"" (https://huggingface.co/abr-ai/niagara-19m-batch.en/blob/dab6545337495482f2fc05455432a7a05c88d3cc/model.py); the repo ships both asr-19m-v2-en-cpu.pt and asr-19m-v2-en-cuda.pt. Command: card "Install requirements" (pip install datasets torch torchcodec transformers sentencepiece) and "Automatically instantiate the model" / "Transcribing using Python" (features = feature_extractor(audio); logits = model(features); tokenizer.decode_from_logits(logits)) as a uv one-liner, reading a local 16 kHz mono wav with soundfile (card: "This model accepts 16000 Hz Mono-channel Audio (wav files)") instead of the LibriSpeech streaming sample. The repo was renamed (abr-ai/asr-19m-v2-en -> abr-ai/niagara-19m-batch.en) and replaced by a new model on 2026-04-07, so the snapshot is pinned with hf download --revision and loaded from the local directory: passing revision= to from_pretrained is not enough, because model.py fetches the weights with "cached_file(self.model_name_or_path, filename)" without a revision (it would look on main, where these files no longer exist), while the local-directory branch ("if os.path.isdir(self.model_name_or_path)") reads them from the snapshot; tokenization.py has the same branch. Identity: the Open ASR Leaderboard runner (open_asr_leaderboard abr/run_abr.sh, added 2025-11-17) evaluated "abr-ai/asr-19m-v2-en-32b". The two files kept at dab6545 have the same LFS sha256 (cfe6595e02c457b0... cpu, e8dcb36fa1e9c1f3... cuda) as asr-19m-v2-en-32b-cpu.pt / -cuda.pt at commits 36da8c7 (2025-11-18) and 8da6334 (2025-11-20, which added the card model-index with these WERs); commit 8f68d03 (2026-02-27, "Remove 32b from model name") only renamed them. The first upload's single asr-19m-v2-en-32b.pt (b6fa8bc) has the same 722 tensor entries, all equal in size and CRC32 except 97 eight-byte scalars. fp32: 78,083,996 B of tensors for the card's "~19m parameters" (about 4 bytes each). gb is the size of the weight file the command loads (asr-19m-v2-en-cpu.pt 0.08 GB; on CUDA it loads asr-19m-v2-en-cuda.pt, 82,676,054 B); runtime memory is higher. hf download fetches both files (0.17 GB). Licence: ABR open license (card "license: other"). transformers is unpinned as on the card. Not executed here.

identity_note: State-space ASR model; CSV entry 'abr-ai/asr-19m-v2-en-32b'. The repo was renamed (now abr-ai/niagara-19m-batch.en) and replaced with a 'New model version' on 2026-04-07, after this evaluation. variants.cmd: pip install 'transformers>=4.39.0' 'deepspeed>=0.14.2' accelerate && python -c "import torch; from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer; from deepspeed.linear.config import QuantizationConfig; r='Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-instruct'; t=AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(r, trust_remote_code=True); m=AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(r, trust_remote_code=True, low_cpu_mem_usage=True, device_map='auto', ds_quantization_config=QuantizationConfig(q_bits=8), max_memory={i: '150GiB' for i in range(8)}, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16); x=t.apply_chat_template([{'role': 'user', 'content': '5x + 35 = 7x - 60 + 10. Solve for x'}], add_generation_prompt=True, return_tensors='pt').to('cuda'); print(t.decode(m.generate(input_ids=x, max_new_tokens=256)[0]))"

variants.cmd: pip install 'git+https://github.com/huggingface/transformers.git@v4.49.0-AyaVision' torch accelerate && python -c "import torch; from transformers import AutoProcessor, AutoModelForImageTextToText; r='CohereLabs/aya-vision-32b'; p=AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(r); m=AutoModelForImageTextToText.from_pretrained(r, device_map='auto', torch_dtype=torch.float16); i=p.apply_chat_template([{'role': 'user', 'content': [{'type': 'image', 'url': 'https://pbs.twimg.com/media/Fx7YvfQWYAIp6rZ?format=jpg&name=medium'}, {'type': 'text', 'text': 'What does the text in the image say?'}]}], padding=True, add_generation_prompt=True, tokenize=True, return_dict=True, return_tensors='pt').to(m.device); g=m.generate(**i, max_new_tokens=300, do_sample=True, temperature=0.3); print(p.tokenizer.decode(g[0][i['input_ids'].shape[-1]:], skip_special_tokens=True))"

uv run --with torch --with diffusers --with transformers --with accelerate --with safetensors python -c "from diffusers import StableDiffusionPipeline; p=StableDiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained('CompVis/stable-diffusion-v1-3').to('mps'); p.enable_attention_slicing(); p('A lighthouse at sunset', height=512, width=512).images[0].save('image.png')"

variants.note: stable-diffusion.cpp sd-cli, which its README lists with CPU, Metal, CUDA and Vulkan backends (prebuilt binaries on the releases page); download the listed files into models/. Files: sd-v1-3.ckpt 4.27 GB (CompVis/stable-diffusion-v-1-3-original@3d1f90b). gb 2.1 = the ~2.1G that the stable-diffusion.cpp quantization doc gives for Stable Diffusion 1.x q8_0 txt2img at 512x512 (https://github.com/leejet/stable-diffusion.cpp/blob/3f8527a46c54ecf4cb4ed6003da8e8982283c73c/docs/quantization_and_gguf.md); higher than the 1.2 × weights + 0.5 GB rule. Command: the docs/sd.md txt2img example plus --type q8_0, which the quantization doc says converts weights while loading.

name: Lumina-DiMOO

identity_note: Alpha-VLLM/Lumina-DiMOO (single released checkpoint; HF revision f014549, created 2025-09-09, Apache-2.0; technical report arXiv 2510.06308). Unified discrete-diffusion model for generation, editing and understanding. No local command recorded (runs through the authors' repository scripts).

name: OneCAT-3B

identity_evidence.note: App. D: autoregressive unified model

identity_note: onecat-ai/OneCAT-3B (the only released OneCAT checkpoint; HF revision a67e66a, created 2025-09-06, Apache-2.0; report arXiv 2509.03498; contact address at meituan.com). Decoder-only autoregressive unified understanding/generation/editing model. No local command recorded.
params_note: Modality-MoE: 9B total, 3B activated, as the makers' report (Table 2) states for OneCAT-3B (Qwen2.5-3B-instruct base with FFNs replicated per modality); whether the image detokenizer is counted is not stated.

identity_note: nvidia/ChronoEdit-14B (also published as nvidia/ChronoEdit-14B-Diffusers, same weights; card at revision 26b33e0: ~1.4e10 parameters, released on Hugging Face 2025-10-29, governed by the NVIDIA Open Model License). name: Tacotron 2 + WaveGlow (NVIDIA)

variants.cmd: pip install torch numpy scipy librosa unidecode inflect && apt-get update && apt-get install -y libsndfile1 && python -c "import torch; from scipy.io.wavfile import write; tacotron2 = torch.hub.load('NVIDIA/DeepLearningExamples:torchhub', 'nvidia_tacotron2', model_math='fp16', trust_repo=True); tacotron2 = tacotron2.to('cuda'); tacotron2.eval(); waveglow = torch.hub.load('NVIDIA/DeepLearningExamples:torchhub', 'nvidia_waveglow', model_math='fp16', trust_repo=True); waveglow = waveglow.remove_weightnorm(waveglow); waveglow = waveglow.to('cuda'); waveglow.eval(); utils = torch.hub.load('NVIDIA/DeepLearningExamples:torchhub', 'nvidia_tts_utils', trust_repo=True); sequences, lengths = utils.prepare_input_sequence(['Hello world, I missed you so much.']); torch.set_grad_enabled(False); mel, _, _ = tacotron2.infer(sequences, lengths); audio = waveglow.infer(mel); write('audio.wav', 22050, audio[0].data.cpu().numpy())"
variants.note: torch.hub entrypoints on the NVIDIA/DeepLearningExamples 'torchhub' branch (@a6c678e), as documented on the PyTorch Hub Tacotron 2 page. Platform evidence: hub page front matter "accelerator: cuda" and "tacotron2 = tacotron2.to('cuda')" (https://github.com/pytorch/hub/blob/c3beaae7d32fca2a23fec30aa7938ef5c9b6e5d5/nvidia_deeplearningexamples_tacotron2.md); the entrypoint calls "ckpt = torch.load(ckpt_file)" with no map_location and the checkpoint's tensors are stored on cuda:0 (read from the pickle header of a range request), so a CUDA GPU is required (https://github.com/NVIDIA/DeepLearningExamples/blob/a6c678ef0323cdaae053e9eed34dce94488ad313/PyTorch/SpeechSynthesis/Tacotron2/tacotron2/entrypoints.py). Command: the hub page's install line plus torch, chained with &&, then its Python cells joined into python -c with 'with torch.no_grad()' replaced by torch.set_grad_enabled(False) and the notebook IPython playback dropped; trust_repo=True added because current torch.hub.load defaults to trust_repo="check" and prompts for repositories outside its trusted owners (facebookresearch, facebookincubator, pytorch, fairinternal) (https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/e57e6b2367701e4397ea54abf22e97cf80061d9a/torch/hub.py). model_math='fp16' only selects the AMP-trained checkpoints; the entrypoints do not cast to half, and the stored tensors are FloatStorage. gb is the sum of the weight files the command loads (nvidia_tacotron2pyt_fp16_20190427 0.11 GB from tacotron2_pyt_ckpt_amp 19.09.0; nvidia_waveglowpyt_fp16_20190427 1.07 GB from waveglow_ckpt_amp 19.09.0, sizes from the NGC files API: https://api.ngc.nvidia.com/v2/models/nvidia/waveglow_ckpt_amp/versions/19.09.0/files); runtime memory is higher. Identity: Tacotron 2 is NGC tacotron2_pyt_ckpt_amp (the catalogue's licence source) version 19.09.0 (1500 epochs); NGC also holds 19.12.0 (6000 epochs), and neither the FastPitch README MOS table nor the hub page says which Tacotron 2 or WaveGlow checkpoint the MOS used. The WaveGlow here is waveglow_ckpt_amp 19.09.0 (its stored config has WN n_channels 512, read from the pickle header), not the 256-channel waveglow_ckpt_amp_256 used by the FastPitch examples. Checkpoint pickles contain only OrderedDict and tensor-rebuild globals, so torch's weights_only default does not block them. apt-get needs root.

identity_note: Exact NVIDIA implementation with WaveGlow vocoder. Do not transfer these listening-study values to Coqui, SpeechBrain, HiFi-GAN or a differently trained checkpoint. Historical run dependencies documented upstream; no current one-command run verified.

name: UNO

variants.quant: fp8 FLUX.1-dev base + UNO LoRA, CPU offload
variants.cmd: git clone https://github.com/bytedance/UNO.git && cd UNO && pip install -e . && python inference.py --prompt "A clock on the beach is under a red sun umbrella" --image_paths "assets/clock.png" --width 704 --height 704 --offload --model_type flux-dev-fp8
variants.note: README Quick Start install ('pip install -e .  # for who wanna to run the demo/inference only') and its first Inference example, with the low-memory flags: the README says 'For low vmemory usage, please pass the --offload and --name flux-dev-fp8 args. The peak memory usage will be 16GB' (for app.py); inference.py at the pinned commit takes the same switches as --offload and --model_type flux-dev-fp8 (InferenceArgs: offload: bool, model_type: Literal['flux-dev', 'flux-dev-fp8', 'flux-schnell']). gb is that README peak figure, not the estimation rule. Checkpoints (FLUX.1-dev, xflux T5 and CLIP encoders, UNO LoRA dit_lora.safetensors 1.91 GB) download on first run, 37 GB on disk per the README; FLUX.1-dev is a gated repo that needs a Hugging Face login with its licence accepted. Subject-driven generation: needs a reference image (assets/clock.png ships with the repo). Command not executed.

identity_note: UNO (Wu et al., 'Less-to-More Generalization: Unlocking More Controllability by In-Context Generation', arXiv 2504.02160; ByteDance Intelligent Creation Team), a subject-driven multi-reference generator trained from FLUX.1-dev and released in April 2025 as a single LoRA checkpoint (bytedance-research/UNO, dit_lora.safetensors). It is the only UNO release; OmniGen2 report Table 4 cites it as 'UNO [97]' and ImagenWorld Table 2 as 'UNO (Wu et al., 2025c)'. Parameter count not stated by the makers (LoRA on the 12B FLUX.1-dev transformer), so params_b is left out. variants.cmd: pip install "kokoro @ git+https://github.com/Oddadmix/kokoro.git@main" torch soundfile huggingface_hub misaki camel-tools && camel_data -i disambig-mle-calima-msa-r13 && wget https://gist.githubusercontent.com/Oddadmix/dc699f7942a9516ce29d4842c7aed756/raw/827b541c892a862f9ef3b44006a6e27b100d1bdd/arabic_g2p.py && python -c "import numpy as np, torch, soundfile as sf; from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download; from arabic_g2p import ArabicG2P, EXTRA_SYMBOLS, clean_phonemes, normalize_text; from kokoro import KModel, KPipeline; from kokoro import pipeline as kpipeline_mod; R = 'oddadmix/Nabra-82M-v0.1'; kmodel = KModel(repo_id=R, config=hf_hub_download(R, 'config.json'), model=hf_hub_download(R, 'kokoro_arabic.pth'), disable_complex=True).eval(); kmodel.vocab.update(EXTRA_SYMBOLS); kpipeline_mod.LANG_CODES.setdefault('ar', 'ar'); pipeline = KPipeline(lang_code='ar', repo_id=R, model=kmodel); _orig_g2p = pipeline.g2p; pipeline.g2p = lambda t: (clean_phonemes(_orig_g2p(t)[0]), _orig_g2p(t)[1]); voice = torch.load(hf_hub_download(R, 'af_msa.pt'), map_location='cpu', weights_only=True); text_norm, _ = normalize_text('مرحبا بك في نبرة'); diac = ArabicG2P(diacritize=True).diacritize(text_norm); sf.write('nabra.wav', np.concatenate([a.detach().cpu().numpy() for _, _, a in pipeline(diac, voice=voice, speed=1.0)]).astype(np.float32), 24000)"

name: EMA Lightning

name: MMS TTS Turkish
params_note: 36M as printed (HF safetensors metadata 36,285,552).

variants.cmd: uv run --python 3.11 --with transformers --with torch --with scipy python -c "from transformers import VitsModel, AutoTokenizer; import torch, scipy; model = VitsModel.from_pretrained('facebook/mms-tts-tur'); tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('facebook/mms-tts-tur'); inputs = tokenizer('Merhaba, nasılsınız?', return_tensors='pt'); torch.set_grad_enabled(False); output = model(**inputs).waveform; scipy.io.wavfile.write('out.wav', rate=model.config.sampling_rate, data=output.squeeze().numpy())"
variants.note: transformers VitsModel usage from the pinned model card (same snippet as the catalogued mms-tts-amh entry, with the Turkish repo and text). gb: model.safetensors is 145,231,352 bytes (repo tree at the pinned revision); runtime memory is higher. Command not executed.

identity_note: Meta's Massively Multilingual Speech VITS checkpoint for Turkish, facebook/mms-tts-tur (pinned 7e36447, CC BY-NC 4.0). The Antalia re-run loads VitsModel.from_pretrained('facebook/mms-tts-tur') (harness/systems/run_mms.py).
